newsitem.title: INDIA: India's east coast hit by cyclone, 50 dead.
newsitem.headline: India's east coast hit by cyclone, 50 dead.

text.p: A cyclone struck India's east coast with powerful winds and heavy rains Wednesday night, destroying crops, flattening homes and killing about 50 persons, authorities said.
"The devastation there is horrible," an official involved in relief operations said on Thursday. In East Godavari district 100,000 houses were fully or partially damaged.
Andhra Pradesh state officials, who earlier estimated the number of dead at 20, said they expected the death toll to rise further.

The cyclone, which was accompanied by gales of around 100 to 120 kmh (62.5 mph to 75 mph), crossed the coastline 50 km (31 miles) south of the port of Kakinada, wreaking havoc in the rich rice-growing districts of East and West Godavari.

"The system (depression) is weakening," C.V.V. Bhadram, director of the Meteorological Centre, said. He said it was located close to the town of Khammam in the interior Telangana region and was likely to move west and north.

The storm severely hit transport, communications and electricity supplies around East and West Godavari districts and devastated crops in one of India's prime rice-growing areas. Cotton and oilseeds are grown further inland.
The government has asked the military to help with relief operations, officials said.
Last month, floods damaged 1.13 million hectares (3.1 million acres) of land, about eight per cent of farmed areas in the agriculturally fertile state of Andhra Pradesh.
